verdicts.reason: Both make the legal fine print a five-line block at the left that weighs as much as the headline, and both reduce SUNSET SALE to an illegible speck. A at least keeps the tagline as one tiny line under the CTA. B crams the tagline into a narrow five-line column of unreadable words between the can and 30% OFF, and lets SUNSET SALE collide with a background circle at the bottom edge.

A puts the CTA first, which breaks the reading order. Its tagline is an unreadable sliver jammed against the top-left edge, the can is pushed off the bottom so only cropped shapes remain, and the legal block on the right is oversized. B, the same layout as 1B, has the narrow tagline column of illegible words, a dominant legal block and a near-invisible SUNSET SALE. A is marginally less cluttered.

Both use a heavy legal block at the left, a tiny can, and a tagline as an unreadable line jammed against the top-right edge above the CTA. A's SUNSET SALE is illegibly small but sits cleanly under the headline. In B, SUNSET SALE is larger but hangs at the bottom edge over a dark ellipse and looks clipped and disconnected, which makes the composition messier.

A is the only candidate that keeps the tagline as a readable line grouped directly under 30% OFF, with SUNSET SALE beneath. Its hierarchy is clear, though leading with the CTA, putting SUNSET SALE below the tagline and keeping an oversized legal block on the right are still flaws. B again squeezes the tagline into a narrow column of illegible words beside the headline, crops the can at the bottom edge, and lets the legal block dominate the right side.
